newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE SAYS READY TO FEND OFF IMMIGRANTS IF NEEDED.
newsitem.headline: GREECE SAYS READY TO FEND OFF IMMIGRANTS IF NEEDED.

text.p: Greece is ready to increase security at its northern border to fend off a possible new wave of illegal immigrants from its troubled Balkan neighbours, government officials said on Wednesday.

The collapse of pyramid investment schemes in Albania that have left hundreds of thousands destitute and a month of mass protests in financially distressed Bulgaria could prompt another influx of economic refugees, they said.

"The ministries responsible have already planned for such an event. Measures are always at a high level -- with joint police and army patrols -- but have not been intensified yet," Macedonia and Thrace Minister Philipos Petsalnikos told reporters in the northern city of Salonika.

Senior government officials told Reuters that security forces would be rushed quickly to boost guards at Greece's rugged northern borderline, that stretches from the Ionian Sea to Turkey, if immigrants started pouring in.
Greece, the only Balkan country to belong to the European Union, has been swamped by hundreds of thousands of illegal refugees from the Balkans since the fall of communism in 1989 and 1990.

The Public Order ministry, which had been asked in June to draw up a plan to better guard the mountainous frontier, came up this week with an operation code-named "Balkanio", which coordinates action between various border authorities.
"The prime mission is to better organise and co-ordinate public services to deal with illegal immigration and the problems it creates," the ministry said in a statement.

Concern that a fresh wave of immigrants would descend on its already taxed economy also prompted Greece to come up with a proposal for the EU to give financial backing to Balkan countries, in a bid to restore stability to the region.

"Greece will make a proposal at the EU's general affairs council on February 24 to financially support Balkan countries such as Albania and Bulgaria," foreign ministry spokesman Costas Bikas said this week.
The plan would call for support from a list of organisations apart from the EU, such as the International Monetary Fund, the European Investment Bank and other investors.
"We are interested in stability in the Balkans and Europe," Bikas said.
